title: Dutch Revolt and the Dutch Republic
summary: In 1568 William of Orange began an armed revolt of the Netherlands against Philip II of Spain, whose heavy taxes and persecution of Protestants had bred resistance. In 1581 the States General renounced Philip, and from 1588 the seven northern provinces carried on as a republic, rare in a Europe of monarchs. Spain recognised its independence at Münster in 1648. Enriched by refugees from the south and by its trading companies, the Republic became a leading European power and lasted until 1795.

uncertainty.note: Revolt from 1568; the Republic from 1588, recognised in 1648 and lasting until 1795 (Canon van Nederland).
